questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electrons with de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ fall on the target in an $X$-ray tube. The cut-off wavelength for the emitted $X$-rays is
questions.solution:
The momentum of striking electrons,

$\text{p} = \dfrac{\text{h}}{\lambda}$

Therefore the kinetic energy of striking electrons,

$\text{K} = \dfrac{p^{2}}{2 \text{m}} = \dfrac{h^{2}}{2 \text{m} {λ}^{2}}$

This is also the maximum energy of $X$-ray photons.

Therefore, $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda0} = \dfrac{\text{h}2}{2\text{m}{λ}^{2}}$ or ${λ}_{0} = \dfrac{2\text{m}{λ}^{2}\text{c}}{h}$

questions.q: For plane electromagnetic waves propagating in the z-direction, which one of the following combinations gives the correct possible direction for $\overset{→}{E}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ field respectively?
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of electromagnetic wave is along $\overset{→}{E} \times \overset{→}{B}$

Also $\overset{→}{E} \cdot \overset{→}{B} = 0$

When $\overset{→}{E}$ is along $- 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j}$

And $\overset{→}{B}$ is along $3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j}$

Then $\overset{→}{E} \times \overset{→}{B} = \left(-2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j}\\right)\times\left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j}\right)

$= 4\overset{^}{k} + 9\overset{^}{k}$

$= 13\overset{^}{k}$ is along +ve direction also \overset{→}{E} \cdot \overset{→}{B} =0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A laser beam is sent to the moon and reflected back to earth by a mirror placed on the moon by an astronaut. If the moon is at $3, 84, 000km$& distance from earth, how long does it take the light to make the round trip?
questions.solution:
Given:
The& distance of the moon $( s ) = 384000\text{km}$

$= 384000 \times {10}^{3} \text{m}$

We known speed of light $( c ) = 3 \times {10}^{8} \text{m/s}$

Total time taken by the laser beam to make the round trip is

$t = \dfrac{2s}{c} = \dfrac{2 \times 384000 \times 1000}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = 2.5s$

questions.q: About $5 %$of the power of $100W$ light bulb is converted to visible radiation. What is the average intensity of visible radiation at a distance of $10m$? Assume that the radiation is emitted& isotropically and neglect reflection.
options:
$4 \times {10}^{- 3}Wm^{- 2}$
&

$6 \times {10}^{- 3}Wm^{- 2}$
&

$7 \times {10}^{- 3}Wm^{- 2}$
&
questions.solution:
Total power = 100 W

Visible radiation power = 5% of total power

$= \dfrac{5}{100} \times 100 = 5W$

At a distance of 10 m, the energy distributed in the form of sphere Area of sphere = 4\pi (radius)^{2}

The intensity of visible radiation

$= \dfrac{\text{Power}}{\text{Area}}= \dfrac{5}{4 \times 3 \cdot 14\left(10\right)^{2}} = 4 \times 1{0}^{- 3}Wm^{- 2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is equal to
questions.solution:
The speed of light in the vacuum is given by the formula

$c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{\mu}_{0}{ε}_{0}}}$

Where, ${\mu}_{0} =$ permeability of vacuum or air

${ε}_{0} =$ permittivity of air.

Cut-off wavelength of the continuous $X$-rays depends on the atomic number of the target

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $υ = \text{3.0 MHz}$ passes from vacuum into a dielectric medium with permittivity $ε = \text{4.0}$. Then
options: wavelength is doubled and the frequency remains unchanged
wavelength is doubled and frequency becomes half
wavelength is halved and frequency remains unchanged
wavelength and frequency both remain unchanged
questions.solution:
During propagation of a wave from one medium to another, the frequency remains constant and wavelength changes.

$\mu = \sqrt{\dfrac{ε}{ε0}} = \sqrt{4} = 2$

Since $\mu ∝ \dfrac{1}{λ}$

$∴$Wavelength is halved
Hence option (wavelength is halved and frequency remains unchanged) holds good.
